name: SC-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 district with long-serving incumbent Jim Clyburn running for reelection
Strong incumbent fundraising advantage ($1.2M raised, $1.6M on hand vs. unknown challenger totals)
Prediction markets price Clyburn at ~97% to win
No polling or expert ratings, so forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The baseline model's D+22 margin aligns with the district's D+13 lean plus incumbency and money advantages, and Polymarket's 97% Democratic pricing corroborates a Safe D rating. No evidence justifies moving away from the prior.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Clyburn under 60% or a well-funded challenger surge would warrant revisiting, though this is unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 6th District is a majority-Black, Democratic-leaning seat that Jim Clyburn has held since 1993. He is running for reelection with a large financial advantage, having raised over $1.2 million and holding $1.6 million on hand, while Republican John Peterson's fundraising is not reported. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race.

The forecast relies on fundamentals: a D+13 partisan lean, a pro-Democratic national environment, incumbency, and Clyburn's money edge, producing an expected margin of roughly D+22. Prediction markets give Clyburn about a 97% chance of winning, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating.
